observation_summary: The method ArrayUtils.addAll throws an unhandled ArrayStoreException when attempting to concatenate arrays of incompatible types, rather than providing a clear, expected exception.
reasoning_summary: The fix introduces a try-catch block around the array copy operation to validate the compatibility of the array types. By catching the ArrayStoreException and checking if the component types are assignable, the code now correctly validates the input data and throws an IllegalArgumentException when a type mismatch occurs. This is a classic case of adding a missing validation check to handle an edge case in input data.
evidence_used: The fix adds a try-catch block around System.arraycopy.
The catch block checks if type1.isAssignableFrom(type2) to validate compatibility.
The fix throws an IllegalArgumentException when types are incompatible, which is a validation/guard pattern.
The bug report states: 'It would be a lot clearer if the method threw an IlegalArgumentException or similar.'

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The core issue is not the algorithm itself (the array copy is correct for compatible types), but the lack of a guard/validation check to handle incompatible types gracefully.
